info.name: TaskNest API
info.description:
TaskNest – Project Management SaaS REST API (B7A6). Roles: **ADMIN**, **MANAGER**, **MEMBER**.

**Run it:** pick the environment (local or production), then use *Run collection*. The requests are in order: logins save tokens and created ids into collection variables, so later requests use them automatically.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` (set per request from the saved tokens).

**Responses:** success `{ success: true, message, data, meta? }` · error `{ success: false, message, errors: [{ field, message }] }`.

**Demo accounts:** admin@tasknest.com / Admin@12345 · manager@tasknest.com / Manager@123 · rahim@tasknest.com / Member@123 · karim@tasknest.com / Member@123.

Every request has a saved example response recorded from the real API (tokens redacted; SSLCommerz simulated for the payment examples).

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description:
Email/password and Google login. Login requests save the tokens into collection variables automatically, so the next requests just work.

- Access token: 15 minutes, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Refresh token: 7 days, rotated on every use; using an old one again ends all sessions.

Demo accounts: `admin@tasknest.com` / `Admin@12345`, `manager@tasknest.com` / `Manager@123`, `rahim@tasknest.com` / `Member@123`.

request.description: Public. Open `{{baseUrl}}/auth/google?role=MANAGER` in a **browser**: it redirects to Google; after sign-in Google calls the callback below, which answers with the tokens as JSON. `role` (MANAGER or MEMBER) is used only for a new account. Answers 503 when Google is not configured on the server.
Called by Google (not by you). It checks the `state` cookie set by the request above, exchanges the code and verifies Google's ID token. Called directly like this it answers 400.

item.name: 5. Payments (SSLCommerz)
item.description:
PRO plan: 500 BDT for 30 days, no project or member limits.

Real flow: 1) `Start PRO payment` returns `paymentUrl`; 2) open it in a browser and pay with an SSLCommerz sandbox card; 3) SSLCommerz redirects to `/payments/success` and also calls `/payments/ipn`; 4) TaskNest checks `val_id` with the SSLCommerz validation API (status, tran_id, amount, currency) and only then marks the payment PAID and extends the plan, once, in one transaction.

The callback requests here show what SSLCommerz sends. Called by hand they only succeed with a real `val_id` from a sandbox payment.

request.description: MANAGER. The FREE plan allows 2 active projects.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description: A third active project on the FREE plan answers 402 Payment Required.

response.name: 402 Payment Required

request.description: MANAGER. Saves a PENDING payment (amount from the server: 500.00 BDT) and opens an SSLCommerz session. Open `paymentUrl` in a browser to pay. 503 when the store is not configured.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description: Public, called by SSLCommerz (browser redirect). Validated server-to-server with `val_id`; replays and the IPN never extend the plan twice. Set `valId` to the `val_id` SSLCommerz sent to try it by hand.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: After the payment the limit is gone.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description: MANAGER. A second payment, used by the cancel callback below.

response.name: 201 Created
